LLM_description:
To: Executive Supply Chain Leadership  
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director  
Date: To be set  
Subject: Balancing transportation spend and carbon for warehouse-to-store shipments

Context
Transportation is a material driver of our cost structure and our carbon footprint. Our warehouse-to-store network offers many routing choices, and each route carries two distinct signals: the money we pay per unit moved and the emissions produced per unit moved. In practice, the lowest-dollar routes are often the highest emitters, while cleaner options can be more expensive. To protect margins and advance our climate commitments, we will evaluate shipping plans that balance both outcomes rather than optimizing for only one.

Operational rules we must respect
- Route activation and setup charges: Every warehouse-to-store route we choose to use triggers a setup charge (e.g., contracts, paperwork, dock preparation). This charge applies regardless of how much we ship on that route. We should only open routes that meaningfully contribute to demand coverage, cost control, or emissions reduction.
- Minimum order quantities on active routes: Carriers require full-load efficiency. If we activate a route, we must ship at least the defined minimum quantity on it. Activating a route without clearing this threshold is not permissible.
- Limits on the number of supplying warehouses per store: To manage receiving capacity and vendor complexity, each store can be served by no more than a set number of warehouses over the planning horizon.

Network realities
- Warehouses have finite inventory available for outbound shipments. We cannot plan volumes that exceed what is on hand or allocated for this period.
- Stores have minimum demand requirements that must be met to protect in-stock levels and revenue.
- Variable shipping economics and emissions vary by route due to distance, mode, and carrier performance. Some corridors will be clearly cheaper, others clearly cleaner; most will involve trade-offs.

Management priority
Leadership has set explicit importance weights for financial cost and emissions when we evaluate options. We will apply these weights to the per-unit shipping spend and per-unit emissions across all routes. In addition, we will include all route setup charges in full for any route we activate; these charges are not scaled by the weights. This approach ensures our plan mirrors how we want to trade off budget and sustainability while accounting for the step-change cost of opening a route.

Business goal
Identify the set of routes to activate and the volumes to move on each active route such that:
- We do not exceed warehouse inventories.
- Every store’s minimum demand is satisfied.
- Any route we open ships at least its required minimum quantity.
- Each store receives from no more than the allowable number of warehouses.
- The combined score—comprised of weighted variable transportation spend and weighted emissions, plus all setup charges for activated routes—is as low as possible under the above rules.

Outcome and use
The output will be a practical shipping plan that lists which routes to open and the shipment quantities by route. It will also provide total transportation spend, total emissions, and a clear view of the trade-offs inherent in the chosen plan (e.g., what we pay or emit to add or remove a route). Once validated, we will brief regional operations and carrier partners, then schedule execution according to load build and dock availability.
